question: Same task and population class: MCI against healthy controls, in both cases a clinic MCI sample (Noor Hospital, Isfahan, amnestic MCI, for P-117; Moscow Memory Clinic for P-99). The channel differs: resting-state EEG (P-117, Aljalal et al. 2024, correct file downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809423008959-main.pdf) against structural-MRI FreeSurfer morphometry (P-99). Condition 1 fails on the channel.

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-selected channels), 10-fold CV over 3660 EEG segments from 61 participants (29 aMCI, 32 HC). No interval is reported. Wilson with n = 61: z^2/n = 0.06298; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06298 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].

matched_figure_check: None exists. P-117 reports no MRI result and P-99 no EEG result.
performance_validity: The Section 3.5 exclusion applies to P-117 on its own source: 99.81% (>= 0.97), internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segments of 61 participants, no external cohort. P-99 (73%) is not near ceiling.
reason: Both papers classify MCI against healthy controls, and the intervals do not overlap (P-117 [0.937, 1.000], P-99 [0.666, 0.786]). The channel differs, though: EEG against structural MRI (condition 1). P-117's figure is a near-ceiling internal estimate on 61 participants with segment-level cross-validation and no external cohort, the Section 3.5 exclusion (condition 5). The pair does not qualify.

quotes.quote: We assess the classification performance of the proposed methods on 19-channel EEGs recorded from 32 healthy subjects and 29 MCI patients in the resting state.
With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training

The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia). The morphometric data were extracted from T1-weighted structural MR images.
We propose a machine learning method, which achieved an accuracy of 73%
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)
